what_its_for: Cemiplimab-rwlc is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of skin cancer (cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma and basal cell carcinoma) and non-small cell lung cancer. It works by helping your immune system recognize and attack cancer cells. Your doctor will decide if this medicine is right for your type and stage of cancer.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into a vein by a nurse or healthcare provider at a clinic or hospital. You will NOT give this medicine to yourself at home. Each infusion takes about 30 minutes. Stay at the clinic for monitoring after your infusion as directed by your care team.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 350 mg given once every 3 weeks as an IV infusion. Your doctor may adjust your dose or schedule based on how you respond to treatment or if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss or need to reschedule an infusion appointment, call your doctor or clinic right away to set up a new appointment as soon as possible. Do not try to make up a missed dose on your own. Your care team will help you get back on schedule safely.
storage: This medicine is stored and prepared by healthcare professionals at the clinic or hospital. You do not need to store it at home. If you are given any take-home materials or supplies, follow the storage instructions provided by your healthcare team.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting treatment. Avoid taking corticosteroids (like prednisone) or other medicines that suppress your immune system unless your doctor specifically tells you to, as they may interfere with how this medicine works. Do not receive any live vaccines during treatment without first talking to your doctor. Avoid becoming pregnant during treatment — use effective birth control during therapy and for at least 4 months after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience any of the following warning signs of serious immune-related side effects: new or worsening cough, chest pain, or shortness of breath; severe diarrhea or stomach pain; yellowing of skin or eyes (signs of liver problems); skin rash, blistering, or peeling; unusual headaches, confusion, or vision changes; muscle weakness or joint pain; signs of hormone problems such as extreme tiredness, weight gain or loss, or feeling unusually hot or cold; signs of kidney problems such as decreased urination or blood in urine; or any infusion reaction symptoms such as chills, flushing, dizziness, or trouble breathing during or after your infusion.
when_it_works: Cemiplimab-rwlc does not work overnight. Some patients may begin to see results within a few weeks to months, but it can take longer for others. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular exams and imaging tests. Continue all scheduled appointments even if you do not feel immediate changes. Do not stop treatment without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use if you are pregnant. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for at least 4 months after the last dose. Older Adults: No specific dose adjustment is needed based on age alone, but tell your doctor about all your health conditions. Children: Safety and effectiveness in patients under 18 years old has not been established. Organ Transplant Recipients: Tell your doctor if you have had an organ transplant, as this medicine may cause organ rejection. Autoimmune Conditions: Tell your doctor if you have an autoimmune disease (such as lupus, Crohn's disease, or rheumatoid arthritis) before starting treatment, as this medicine may make those conditions worse.
